item.title: Emergency drinking water delivered to Cikobia District School as tanks reach critically low levels
item.description: Emergency drinking water has been delivered to Cikobia District School after severe dry weather linked to ongoing El Niño conditions left the island’s main rainwater catchment tanks at critically low levels. The Fiji Red Cross Society Northern Division team delivered 50 cartons of bottled water to the remote school, providing immediate drinking water for 25 students and four teachers.
item.content:encoded:
Emergency drinking water has been delivered to Cikobia District School after severe dry weather linked to ongoing El Niño conditions left the island’s main rainwater catchment tanks at critically low levels.

The Fiji Red Cross Society Northern Division team delivered 50 cartons of bottled water to the remote school, providing immediate drinking water for 25 students and four teachers.

The team travelled by boat with Provincial Administrator Macuata and his team on Thursday and reached Cikobia Island on Friday.

The assistance follows an urgent request from the school’s head as the water shortage threatened the health, hygiene and daily operations of the school.

The Fiji Red Cross says the water supply is expected to provide a 24-day buffer while government water cartage operations are arranged to reach the island.

Cikobia District School serves children from four surrounding villages — Vatulele, Nautovatu, Vuninuku and Nalele.

The Fiji Red Cross says the emergency assistance will help ensure students and teachers have access to safe drinking water while the island continues to experience dry conditions.

item.title: Youth urged to walk together for a more united Fiji
item.description: Fiji’s young people are being urged to stand together, respect differences and use their voices to build a more united and peaceful country. Permanent Secretary for Justice and Acting Permanent Secretary for the Ministry of Women, Children and Social Protection, Selina Kuruleca, stated this at the Walk With Me Interfaith Youth Concert at the FMF Gymnasium in Suva last night.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji’s young people are being urged to stand together, respect differences and use their voices to build a more united and peaceful country.

Permanent Secretary for Justice and Acting Permanent Secretary for the Ministry of Women, Children and Social Protection, Selina Kuruleca, stated this at the Walk With Me Interfaith Youth Concert at the FMF Gymnasium in Suva last night.

About 2000 youths came to the concert, which brought together young people from different faiths and communities through music, friendship and fellowship.

Kuruleca, who was the Chief Guest, says young people have an important role to play in Fiji through education, faith, community service, leadership, sports and entrepreneurship.

She says while young people face challenges such as drugs, violence and pressure from social media, these challenges should not define their generation.

Kuruleca says the theme “Walk With Me” is a call for people from different faiths, cultures and traditions to walk alongside each other with compassion and respect.

She is encouraging young people to learn about each other’s cultures, listen to one another and focus on the values they share.

Kuruleca is also urging young people to become peacebuilders online by thinking carefully before posting, sharing or commenting on social media.

She says their words should be used to build understanding rather than division.

Kuruleca says relationships create understanding, understanding builds trust, and trust is the bedrock of lasting peace.

The free concert was hosted by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and was open to young people aged 12 to 35, regardless of their faith or community.

Before the event, organisers had expected more than 1,000 young Fijians to attend.

The programme featured local youth and young adults performing gospel and worship music, along with inspirational messages focusing on faith , friendship, service and making positive choices.

Kuruleca acknowlegdes the Church for creating a space where young people can meet, learn, serve and lead together, saying such initiatives help strengthen social cohesion in Fiji.

She ended her message by encouraging young people to walk with faith, walk with purpose, walk with compassion, walk with those who are different from them and, above all, walk together.

item.title: Hundreds turn out for Sai Prema Foundation’s free eye screening in Suva
item.description: Hundreds of people have turned up at the Sai Prema Foundations free eye screening camp at the Sanjeevani Medical Centre in Nasese, Suva, to have their vision tested and receive prescription glasses from specialists from the United States and India. Director and CEO of Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Heart Hospital Fiji, Dr Krupali Tappoo says more than 500 people have already registered for the screenin
item.content:encoded:
Hundreds of people have turned up at the Sai Prema Foundations free eye screening camp at the Sanjeevani Medical Centre in Nasese, Suva, to have their vision tested and receive prescription glasses from specialists from the United States and India.

Director and CEO of Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Heart Hospital Fiji, Dr Krupali Tappoo says more than 500 people have already registered for the screening.

Dr Tappoo says people have travelled from Suva, Nausori, Sigatoka, Rakiraki and surrounding areas to access the free service.

The wider outreach began with screenings in six rural villages in Nadi, Dratabu, Saunaka, Yavusania, Sikituru, Navatulevu and Narewa, before moving into schools.

The teams have since screened students across 83 schools in Ba, Lautoka, Nadi, Sigatoka, Suva and Nausori.

She also adds a total of 43,666 eye screenings have been conducted so far, with 1,183 prescription eyeglasses provided free of charge to people identified as needing them.

The outreach team has also provided specialised paediatric cardiac screenings, including echocardiograms, alongside the eye screening programme at participating schools in the West.

She says the initiative aims to make eye care accessible to people who may otherwise struggle to afford or access an eye examination.

Dr Tappoo says vision problems can particularly affect children, as a child who is unable to see clearly in the classroom may sometimes be mistaken for not understanding or grasping their schoolwork.

She says the team is providing reading and distance glasses, while people requiring further assessment or treatment are being referred to eye specialists.

Dr Tappoo says the current Suva screening follows an extensive outreach programme in the Western Division involving a team of about 40 people, including visiting specialists from the United States and India and staff from Sanjeevani Hospital.

Founder of Anekant Community Centre USA, Dr Nitin Shah says people aged 55 and above are initially assessed for possible cataracts, while those who pass the initial assessment undergo further testing using specialised equipment.

Dr Shah says the equipment can provide a prescription within 15 to 30 seconds, while people requiring more complex prescriptions are assessed by optometrists.

He says childrens vision screening is also an important part of the initiative because identifying and correcting vision problems at a young age can make a significant difference to their lives.

Dr Shah says the screening can take about 10 seconds per child, allowing large numbers of students to be screened in a short period.

He says his team has screened about 1.5 million children across 10 countries over the past two years, including about 70,000 children in Fiji during last years and this years programmes.

Dr Tappoo is encouraging people in the Central Division to take advantage of the free service, which will continue tomorrow from 8.30am to 3pm at the Sanjeevani Medical Centre in Nasese, Suva.

item.title: Marist Old Boys launch Road to 90 ahead of 90th anniversary
item.description: Speaking at the 2026 Marist Old Boys Association Annual Bazaar 2026 Family Day, President of the Association, Neumi Vakadewabuka says the anniversary will be an opportunity to honour the legacy of the Marist Brothers and build on the work they started. Vakadewabuka says Marist Brothers High School officially began on 1 February 1937, while the Marist Brothers history in Fiji dates back to 1844 whe
item.content:encoded:
Speaking at the 2026 Marist Old Boys Association Annual Bazaar 2026 Family Day, President of the Association, Neumi Vakadewabuka says the anniversary will be an opportunity to honour the legacy of the Marist Brothers and build on the work they started.

Vakadewabuka says Marist Brothers High School officially began on 1 February 1937, while the Marist Brothers history in Fiji dates back to 1844 when they began their work in Lakeba.

He says the Road to 90 theme is honouring the past, celebrating the present and protecting the future.

Vakadewabuka says the association wants the celebrations to be meaningful and to encourage current students, while also supporting young people who have recently left school and are facing challenges finding employment.

He says a combined fundraiser for works of mercy is planned for December, followed by a combined Mass at the school on 1 February 2027 to mark the exact date the school began.

He says activities will then continue in June, with Marist Old Boys in Nadi starting the celebrations on 4 June 2027, followed by a combined Mass in Suva on 6 June 2027 to mark the feast day.

He is encouraging Marist Old Boys living overseas, including those in the United States, Australia and New Zealand, to make preparations early and be part of the celebrations.

Vakadewabuka says the Marist Old Boys Bazaar is also about supporting and empowering members, with organisations including the Fiji Development Bank, FNPF, LTA, Elections Office and Ministry of Justice providing services at the event.

He says the association is also working with several firms to provide group discounts of between 10 and 15 percent for Marist Old Boys.

A BSP Life Insurance initiative has also been launched, with around 80 people already starting their premiums.

Vakadewabuka says the association is also focused on some of the challenges facing Fiji, particularly drugs and HIV.

The Ministry of Health is at the bazaar providing voluntary HIV and diabetes testing, and he is encouraging members to take advantage of the services.

He says the association wants Marist Old Boys to show how an alumni family can respond to challenges while continuing the legacy of service started by the Marist Brothers.

Vakadewabuka also acknowledged members who have been involved in works of mercy, including feeding the poor, visiting people in need and helping others access medical facilities and financial assistance.

He is encouraging members to keep their families well, remain connected and continue supporting works of mercy as the Marist community moves towards its 90th anniversary.

item.title: 16 vendors bring food, fun and community spirit to GESA Market Day
item.description: GESA Market Day draws strong turnout with 16 vendors and more expected to join todays event. The Gospel High School Ex-Scholars Association (GESA) second Market Day is underway today, with strong support from families and members of the public.
item.content:encoded:
GESA Market Day draws strong turnout with 16 vendors and more expected to join todays event.

The Gospel High School Ex-Scholars Association (GESA) second Market Day is underway today, with strong support from families and members of the public.

GESA Committee Member and Team Lead for Day 1, Raksha Priya, says the event was initially planned to have 13 vendors, but 16 vendors are already taking part, with another five expected to join.

Priya, who is a former Gospel High School student from the 2001 year group and a member of the 65th Sapphire Committee, says todays Market Day was organised following the popularity of last weeks event.

She says the event was scheduled to start at 9am, but vendors were ready early, so it started at 8am.

Priya says the turnout has been good, with families coming together for breakfast and lunch, while some are also buying food to take home for dinner.

She says a range of food and other items are available, including chicken pulao, chicken curry, barbecue, fusion food, cakes and pastries, jewellery and household items.

There is also a coffee corner where people can enjoy tea or coffee, particularly with the cool weather.

Priya says Gospel High School merchandise is also available, including general merchandise and T-shirts for the upcoming march.

She says the Market Day is scheduled to finish at 4pm, although last week’s event saw food sell out by around 12.30pm.

Priya says there are also many other activities planned through to November, with different teams working on various events and activities.

She says while the Market Day is being held today, another team is at the high school cleaning the hall, while other activities are also taking place elsewhere.

Priya is encouraging people in the Suva-Nausori corridor, including those around Samabula, as well as people travelling to or from work, to stop by the Market Day.

She says people are likely to find something they have been craving or something they can look forward to enjoying.

item.title: Man who collapsed near Suva Grammar School identified by relative
item.description: The man who collapsed while on a morning walk near Suva Grammar School this morning has been positively identified by a relative. Police had earlier appealed for the public’s assistance to identify the man after he was rushed to the CWM Hospital, where his death was confirmed.
item.content:encoded:
The man who collapsed while on a morning walk near Suva Grammar School this morning has been positively identified by a relative.

Police had earlier appealed for the public’s assistance to identify the man after he was rushed to the CWM Hospital, where his death was confirmed.

They say a relative has since come forward and identified the victim.

The earlier appeal for information is now cancelled.

Police thank members of the public who shared the initial appeal.

item.title: Lautoka City Council rolls out solar-powered CCTV cameras to boost public safety
item.description: People in Lautoka will have greater access to CCTV surveillance, with the Lautoka City Council installing solar-powered cameras at key locations across the city. The Council says three solar-powered CCTV cameras have so far been installed at Nede Street, Tukani Street and Veve Street.
item.content:encoded:
People in Lautoka will have greater access to CCTV surveillance, with the Lautoka City Council installing solar-powered cameras at key locations across the city.

The Council says three solar-powered CCTV cameras have so far been installed at Nede Street, Tukani Street and Veve Street.

It says the installations are part of efforts to enhance public safety and security across the city.

The Council says the cameras are currently in the testing phase, which will allow it to assess their performance, coverage and effectiveness in the identified areas.

It says a further five solar-powered CCTV cameras are planned to be installed this month , with additional installations to continue progressively each month.

The installations are being carried out under the direction of Acting Chief Executive Officer Taitusi Rasoki Kata.

item.title: Police seek public help to identify man who died after collapsing near Suva Grammar
item.description: Totogo Police are seeking the public’s help to identify a man in his 50s who died after collapsing during a morning walk near Suva Grammar School today. Police say the man was rushed to CWM Hospital after he collapsed, where medical officials confirmed his death.
item.content:encoded:
Totogo Police are seeking the public’s help to identify a man in his 50s who died after collapsing during a morning walk near Suva Grammar School today.

Police say the man was rushed to CWM Hospital after he collapsed, where medical officials confirmed his death.

He is believed to be in his 50s, with short hair and a fair complexion.

At the time, he was wearing a plain black T-shirt, black shorts, black ASICS shoes, Nike socks and a wristwatch.

Police are urging anyone who may know the man or have information that could help identify him to contact the Divisional Police Commander Central on 8904742.
